packs.title: Green and Blue
packs.promise: Explore garden forms, hill landmarks and coastal paths across Singapore.

q.s: Find two different directions in a heritage tree.
st: From a stopped place outside the fence, or in the official photograph, find the tree’s distinctive long lower branch and its higher crown.
Draw two simple direction lines: one following the lower branch and one following an upward branch. Add a word for each direction.
Save the two lines and words. Keep the fence and visitor path clear; seeing the whole tree is more useful than approaching its roots.

q.s: Collect a plant detail and a sourced scent description.
st: Find one visible plant form from an open path, or choose one in the official Fragrant Garden photograph. Describe its shape or texture without touching.
Read the Gardens’ description of this collection. Record one scent-related detail from that source and label it as sourced rather than a scent you personally detected.
Save the visible detail and sourced description. An optional scent observation can be added from the path, but the two-note version earns the same credit.

q.s: Invent a path from a play tower’s exterior curves.
st: Find a curved exterior slide and a repeated horizontal tower edge from a stopped public viewpoint, or in the official photograph.
Invent a small line design inspired by the two forms. Give your drawn route a start, a change of direction and a finish; it is a drawing rather than a route to walk or climb.
Save the original design and name its main change of direction. Do not enter the tower, copy signage or photograph playground users.

packs.title: River in Detail
packs.promise: Read Singapore’s civic streets and waterfront one small detail at a time.

q.s: Let a civic facade speak through shape alone.
st: Choose an open public-sidewalk view of the National Gallery Singapore facade facing the Padang. Interior admission is unnecessary.
Find three different architectural voices: a repeated vertical line, an arch or curve, and a broad flat surface.
Give each a plain descriptive word. Arrange the words from quietest to boldest and note which shape led your choice.

q.s: Pair solid shapes with their softer echoes.
st: Choose a comfortable public path position at Boat Quay, away from restaurant entrances and water access.
Find two pairs: a building shape and its reflection, then a railing or mooring edge and its broken line in the water. If reflections are faint, pair the shape with its shadow.
Write one word for each solid form and one for its softer partner. Which pair looks most different?

q.s: Let two riverbank details start a letter.
st: Choose an open outdoor place near the Asian Civilisations Museum at Empress Place; entering the museum is optional.
Find a detail in the building exterior and a detail in the nearby river or trees.

Write an unsent postcard of exactly two sentences. Begin the first with the building detail and the second with the river or tree detail. Address it to a future version of yourself or leave it unaddressed.
